title: A non-food business's brief (Harbour Sport Club) speaks its trade's words, keeps one copy of each photo and offers three hero candidates, never the logo
steps: S1: Build the brief of Harbour Sport Club's 23 real photos (13 Instagram, 10 Google Places; fixture test/fixtures/pictures/near-copies.json) through fromPlace and makeSiteBrief, with its Instagram profile picture as the chosen logo.
S2: Same with a Google Maps menu photo among the reviews' photos.
S3: Build briefs for a food, a fitness, an unknown-trade and an old food record (no trade, collected menu items).
expect: S1: the brief validates; the three Instagram copies of Google #33, #27, #30 are left out (20 photos remain); the hero section's assetIds are Google #24, #28, #31 (1600 x 2133) and never the logo.
S2: the menu photo leaves the hero candidates and nothing takes its place.
S3: food keeps menu and Book a table wording; fitness reads services and booking; unknown reads offerings; the old food record stays food.
evidence: #1780: Harbour Sport Club, a coaching club, got a restaurant brief (menu, Book a table), the same photo twice (Instagram and Google copies 3, 6 and 12 bits apart) and its logo as the hero picture.
fence: Static: domain and brief-research functions on fixture rows; no database, no model, no stand. The reading seam with Postgres is apps/tracy-web/test/website-opportunities-business-reading.test.mjs.

tests: Harbour Sport Club's hero offers its three largest Google photos, the logo none of them
a Google Maps menu photo leaves the hero candidates, and nothing takes its place
a brief of Harbour Sport Club's 23 photos keeps one copy of each, the sharper Google one
different pictures with close fingerprints all reach the brief
trade words: an old food record without a trade
